thread:
alex: Heads up — seeing a 20–40ms p99 bump on the qwen-mixtral V2 route after the kernel-picker prefetch tweak. Looks correlated with chat templates that include emojis and a bunch of special tokens: ascii-only prompts are fine, mixed UTF-8 triggers regression.

maria: Thanks — are you sure it's the tokenizer causing byte-fallback? any logs?

alex: Quick repro attached inline. Minimal prompt that regresses: `system: You are an assistant.
user: Summarize the following text 😊 — long context...` When the tokenizer emits a lot of byte-fallback tokens we see immediate fallback kernels selected (byte_fallback_kernel) instead of the planned optimized attention kernel. Profiling snippet:```
Kernel selection summary:
  batch=1 seq=512 model=qwen-mixtral-v2
  chosen_kernel: optimized_attn (expected) -> 120ms total
  chosen_kernel: byte_fallback_kernel -> 320ms total

nvprof-like counters:
  optimized_attn: 1 launch, 12ms avg
  byte_fallback_kernel: 1 launch, 48ms avg (per step thrash)
```

sam: that's a big delta. Could the RoPE scaling math be different for the fallback path and forcing extra compute?

jing: Possibly — fallback path uses a different codepath that doesn't reuse the KV head/dim packing, so we might be hitting suboptimal matmul shapes. Also prefetch/route timing matters: if prefetching sees ascii tokens then the runtime picks precompiled kernel; when byte-fallback is discovered at tokenization stage (later), the router has to reassign mid-batch -> kernel swap + cache churn.

priya: Do we have traces showing when tokenization runs vs routing decision? Iirc tokenization used to happen before routing but we introduced lazy-tokenization for small messages to save CPU. That might be the root cause.

alex: Exactly. The recent change delayed tokenization for some codepaths, so kernel picker runs with incomplete token info. If later tokens force byte-fallback, we do immediate (synchronous) fallback and drop into the slower kernel.

perf-bot: ALERT: Canary qwen-mixtral-v2 p99 increased 22% vs 7d baseline; affected routes: /chat, /stream.

maria: Three quick mitigations to try: 1) revert lazy-tokenization for routes that use large system prompts, 2) add a fast pre-tokenization pass that only checks for non-ascii/emoji, 3) extend prefetch window so kernel-picker waits until tokenization checkpoint.

jing: I'll run a quick microbench: disable lazy-tokenization on a canary host, enable verbose kernel-selection logging. Also will add histogram for mid-batch kernel swaps.

sam: Also check KV-cache warmup behavior — if we swap kernels mid-conversation the KV layout might change and cause additional memcpy/regen overhead. That could amplify the latency too.

alex: Confirmed in a deeper trace: mid-batch kernel swap triggers KV rebind path which takes ~30–50ms for the worst case. So total p99 = kernel swap cost + slower per-step kernel.

priya: For model-specific tuning: qwen's head_dim is slightly unusual vs our Llama path. Maybe we should add an explicit kernel override map for qwen-mixtral when tokenization indicates token set X (emoji/special). That avoids the dynamic picker thrash.

maria: Priorities: immediate canary with lazy-tokenization revert (jing), add pre-tokenization check (alex/priya), and longer-term: make kernel-picker aware of tokenization-latency (sam).

alex: I'll push a small canary today and post timings. If canary looks good, we can roll revert and follow with a safer pre-tokenize feature.

jing: Assigned. I'll update this thread with short diffs and perf numbers.

priya: One more note — add telemetry tags: tokenization_path=lazy|eager and kernel_swap=true|false so we can query cause in dashboards.

alex: Agreed. Also let's add a unit test that forces emoji-heavy chat templates to ensure kernel-picker doesn't regress silently.

maria: Nice. Thanks folks.

jing: Quick update: canary disabled lazy-tokenization on 2 hosts -> p99 down from 310ms to 145ms on the canary slice for the repro prompt. Posting logs in a follow-up thread.

alex: Great. Follow-ups: (1) add pre-tokenize check (PR queued), (2) add kernel-picker guardrail to avoid mid-batch swaps when possible, (3) telemetry tags as priya suggested. I'll create JIRA tickets for the last two.

maria: Sounds good. :thumbsup:
